html:
1What You Will Learn

  • The right escalation triggers, and why sentiment and self-reported confidence are poor proxies
  • What to do on an explicit request for a human, on frustration, on policy gaps and on multiple matches
  • Structured error context for multi-agent recovery
  • The two anti-patterns: silent suppression and total abort

2Escalation and Ambiguity (Task 5.2)

Running case

Birchwood Supply's Agent Escalates the Wrong Cases

  • The target is 80%+ first-contact resolution, but the agent reaches only 62%
  • It escalates routine address changes on unshipped orders and tries to handle alone gift-card disputes that need policy exceptions

When to escalate

Escalate when... Notes
The customer explicitly asks for a human Honor it immediately, without first investigating
Policy has an exception or a gap The policy is silent or ambiguous about the request (for example, a price match against a competitor when policy covers only your own site)
The agent cannot make meaningful progress Repeated failed attempts, missing access
Do not escalate only because... Why
The customer sounds frustrated Acknowledge the frustration and offer to resolve if it is within the agent's capability; escalate if the customer repeats the wish for a person
The case looks complex Complexity alone is not the criterion; policy gaps and inability to progress are

Unreliable proxies

  • Sentiment analysis measures mood, not case complexity: a calm customer can have a policy-exception case and an angry one a simple fix.
  • Self-reported confidence scores (1 to 10) are poorly calibrated: the agent is often confidently wrong on exactly the hard cases.
  • Fix the root cause (unclear decision boundaries) with explicit escalation criteria and few-shot examples in the system prompt, showing when to escalate and when to resolve alone. Training a separate classifier is over-engineered before prompt optimization has been tried.

Ambiguity: multiple matches

  • If a tool returns several customers with the same name, ask for an additional identifier (email, phone, order number). Do not pick one by a heuristic (most recent, most orders): a wrong guess exposes another person's data or refunds the wrong account.
Exam tip

Sentiment thresholds and confidence cutoffs are classic wrong answers. The proportionate first step is explicit criteria plus few-shot examples.

Exam tip

Several matching customers → ask for another identifier; never pick one by a heuristic.

3Error Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems (Task 5.3)

Case (continued): The research subagent that searches the web times out on a hard topic. What should reach the coordinator?

Return to the coordinator Why
Failure type (timeout, access denied, rate limited) Decides retry versus alternative
What was attempted (the exact query) Lets it retry with a changed query
Partial results Work already done is not thrown away
Possible alternatives Suggests another source or approach
  • Access failure versus valid empty result: a timeout needs a retry decision; a successful search with no matches is a legitimate answer.
  • Generic statuses such as "search unavailable" hide the context the coordinator needs.
  • Local recovery: the subagent retries transient failures itself and propagates only unresolved errors, with what was attempted and partial results.
Anti-pattern Problem
Silently suppressing errors (return an empty set marked successful) The failure is invisible; the report looks complete but is not
Terminating the whole workflow on one failure Throws away everything that worked when recovery was possible
  • Coverage annotations: the final output should mark which findings are well supported and which areas have gaps because sources were unavailable.
Exam tip

Best answer for a subagent failure = structured error context to the coordinator, then recover or proceed with partial results and annotate gaps.

4Exam Q&A

S1Birchwood's agent escalates routine address changes but tries to settle gift-card disputes that need exceptions by itself. What is the best first improvement?

  • ATrain a separate classifier on old tickets first
  • BAsk the agent to report confidence from 1 to 10 and escalate when it is below 5
  • CEscalate every conversation that includes the word "problem"
  • DAdd explicit escalation criteria with few-shot examples to the system prompt
Show the answer

Answer: D. The root cause is unclear decision boundaries; criteria with examples are the proportionate fix. Self-reported confidence is unreliable and a classifier is heavy infrastructure.

S2A customer writes: "I want to speak to a person." What should the agent do?

  • AEscalate immediately, without investigating first
  • BAsk the customer to explain the problem again before deciding what to do
  • COffer a discount
  • DInvestigate the issue first and then decide
Show the answer

Answer: A. An explicit request for a human is honored at once.

S3A customer sounds irritated about a late parcel but does not ask for a person, and the agent can see the tracking and fix the issue. What is best?

  • AAcknowledge the frustration, offer to resolve it, and escalate only if the customer repeats the wish for a person
  • BEnd the chat
  • CIgnore the tone and give no acknowledgement
  • DEscalate immediately because of the negative tone, so that a person can calm the customer down
Show the answer

Answer: A. Frustration alone is not an escalation trigger when the agent can resolve the issue.

S4A customer asks for a price match with a competitor's website, and the policy covers only adjustments to Birchwood's own prices. What should the agent do?

  • AApprove it to keep the customer happy
  • BEscalate, because the policy is silent on the request
  • CDeny it with a made-up rule
  • DAsk for a coupon code from the competitor and apply it to the order
Show the answer

Answer: B. A policy gap is a legitimate trigger for escalation.

S5A search for customer "Sam Rivera" returns three records. What should the agent do?

  • APick at random
  • BAsk the customer for an additional identifier before proceeding
  • CChoose the most recently active account
  • DRefund all three
Show the answer

Answer: B. With multiple matches, request clarification rather than selecting by heuristic.

S6The web search subagent times out. Which design best allows intelligent recovery?

  • AReturn structured error context with failure type, attempted query, partial results and possible alternatives
  • BReturn an empty result marked successful
  • CStop the whole research workflow
  • DReturn a generic "search unavailable" status once all of the retries have been used up without success
Show the answer

Answer: A. Rich context lets the coordinator retry, change approach or proceed with partial results. A generic status hides it, an empty success hides the failure, and a total stop wastes working parts.

S7Which statement describes a valid empty result?

  • AA completed search that found no matching documents
  • BA permission error
  • CA crashed subagent
  • DA timeout from the search service while it was still looking for documents
Show the answer

Answer: A. An empty result from a successful query is an answer; the others are failures.

S8Where should a final research report show that one region's data could not be retrieved?

  • AIn coverage annotations that mark well-supported findings and gaps
  • BIn a separate email
  • CNowhere; hide it to look complete
  • DIn a footnote that describes the model's reasoning about the missing region
Show the answer

Answer: A. Annotating coverage keeps the report honest about which areas are well supported and which have gaps.

S9Which TWO are valid reasons to escalate to a human? Select TWO.

  • AThe customer explicitly asks for a person
  • BA sentiment score is below a threshold
  • CThe agent's self-reported confidence is below 7
  • DThe policy is silent about the request
  • EThe customer wrote an exclamation mark
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Explicit requests and policy gaps are real triggers. Tone, sentiment scores and self-reported confidence are weak proxies for difficulty.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Escalate when Explicit human request (immediately) · policy gap/exception · no meaningful progress
Frustration only Acknowledge, offer to resolve; escalate if the customer repeats the request
Bad proxies Sentiment and self-reported confidence
Fix calibration Explicit criteria + few-shot examples in the system prompt
Multiple matches Ask for another identifier; no heuristics
Error context Failure type · attempted query · partial results · alternatives
Distinguish Access failure (error, retry decision) vs valid empty result (success, none found)
Anti-patterns Silent suppression; abort everything
Recovery Local retry of transient errors; propagate the unresolved; annotate coverage gaps
